subject.name: Mathematics
subject.description: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics. This sample covers Paper 1 (Pure Mathematics 1) only. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: Quadratics
topics.summary: Completing the square, the discriminant, solving quadratic equations and inequalities.

topics.title: Functions
topics.summary: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations of graphs.

topics.title: Coordinate geometry
topics.summary: Equations of lines and circles, intersections of lines and curves.

topics.title: Circular measure
topics.summary: Radians, arc length and sector area.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Graphs of trigonometric functions, exact values, identities and equations.

topics.title: Series
topics.summary: Binomial expansion, arithmetic and geometric progressions, sum to infinity.

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Gradients, the chain rule, tangents and normals, stationary points, rates of change.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Integration as the reverse of differentiation, definite integrals, areas and volumes of revolution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express 2x² − 12x + 7 in the form a(x + b)² + c. Give your answer in that form.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who first took out the factor of 2 from the x terms were usually successful. A common error was c = −2, from failing to multiply 9 by 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the set of values of k for which the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has no real roots. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the discriminant: k² − 36
M1 for setting k² − 36 < 0 and finding critical values ±6

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the critical values but then gave the incorrect region k < −6, k > 6, or used ≤.

questions.stem: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 for x ∈ ℝ and g(x) = 1/(x + 1) for x > −1.

parts.label: (a)
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found gf(1) instead. fg(x) means apply g first.

markingPoints.text: M1 for a correct first step, e.g. x = 3y − 2

questions.stem: A circle has equation x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the radius of the circle.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates completed the square correctly. Sign errors in the centre were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at the point (6, 2). Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for tangent gradient = −3/4 and use of (6, 2)

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should remember the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.stem: A sector OAB of a circle has centre O, radius 8 cm and angle AOB = 1.2 radians.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of the sector, in cm².

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the area of the segment bounded by the arc AB and the chord AB, in cm², correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for triangle area ½ × 8² × sin 1.2
M1 for sector area − triangle area

parts.examinerComment: A significant number of candidates had their calculators in degree mode, giving sin 1.2° and an incorrect answer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve 2sin²θ − sin θ − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for factorising: (2 sin θ + 1)(sin θ − 1) = 0
A1 for sin θ = 1 giving θ = 90°
A1 for sin θ = −1/2 giving θ = 210°
A1 for θ = 330° and no extra solutions in range

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates factorised correctly. Many lost the final mark by missing 330° or including extra solutions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of tan(π/3) − 2cos(π/6).
parts.examinerComment: Exact values should be recalled rather than found by calculator.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2 − x)⁶.
parts.examinerComment: The negative sign was frequently lost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A geometric progression has first term 24 and common ratio 0.75. Find the sum to infinity.

questions.stem: A curve has equation y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 4.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the stationary points and determine their nature. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using d²y/dx² = 6x − 12 or another valid method

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must give a reason for the nature of each point; stating 'maximum' without justification did not earn the final mark.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate the integral of (6x² − 4x) with respect to x, from x = 1 to x = 3.
parts.examinerComment: Arithmetic errors when substituting the lower limit were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The region bounded by y = √x, the x-axis and the line x = 4 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed, as a multiple of π. Enter the multiple only (e.g. for 5π enter 5).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates integrated √x rather than (√x)². The volume formula requires y².
